bull_bear.body: Share buyback completed (Rs. 4.25 lakh shares, promoter holding up to 63.2%). Dividend reduced to Rs. 1/share (vs Rs. 7.5 last year) due to temporary earnings dip. Future capex to be funded internally/debt only upon new product revenue traction.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Resumption of Chinese dumping if export incentives reintroduced. 2) Volatility in vegetable oil prices (daily revision contracts). 3) Delay in customer validation for new high-margin product (2-2.5 year cycle). 4) Working capital strain (cycle at 100-120 days).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledged 'washed out' last two years but emphasized structural turnaround via dumping cessation and operational efficiencies. Confident on 8% margin target and long-term vision.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management revealed that Chinese dumping ceased likely due to removal of 15% export incentives by Beijing, not just market forces. Also, the new 40kT capacity is not a single block but will be ramped gradually (starting 8kT) to match slow customer validation cycles in cosmetics/specialty sectors.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated governance/financial principles: always be adequately capitalized, not overleverage the balance sheet, secure sources of sustainable raw material supply, invest in backward and forward integration, transparent communications with all stakeholders, and low volatility in cash flow generation.
- Recently concluded buy-back of INR 340 Mn in Jan-26.
- Dividend Percentage shown as 75% for FY24, 75% for FY25 and 10% for FY26.
- Net Debt to Equity shown as 0.02 (FY24), 0.20 (FY25) and 0.32 (FY26); Cash Conversion Cycle Days of 76 (FY24), 99 (FY25) and 128 (FY26).
- Return Ratio chart shows ROCE of 19.08% (FY24), 10.40% (FY25) and 3.88% (FY26) and ROE of 13.97% (FY24), 7.28% (FY25) and 2.09% (FY26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Leadership position in the Indian Dimer Acid market, built on pricing strategy, timely service, quick supply, fair payment terms and quality, against Chinese suppliers as main competitors
- Ability to process by-products with no fixed technical specification into higher-grade fatty acids and intermediate nutraceuticals meeting stringent quality standards
- Strong, long-standing customer and supplier relationships of more than 25 years
- First Indian and reportedly first Asian company to manufacture Isostearic Acid to internationally acceptable quality without importing technology or external consultants, in a field with only 3-4 global manufacturers
- Only Indian company producing the grade of Linoleic Acid needed for superior-grade paints, making it the preferred supplier for that use
- Natural structural barrier to new entrants: limited domestic availability of key raw materials and unviable import economics under prevailing duties make the market suited to essentially one large domestic player
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material availability and import dependence — Management flags availability of the right kinds of raw materials in adequate quantity at fair prices as the main risk; raw materials are by-products of vegetable-oil refineries, and India depends substantially on imports of crude vegetable oils from Indonesia, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Ukraine and Russia, so those countries' export-policy shifts or events such as war can spike raw-material prices that are difficult to pass through to finished-product pricing quickly.
- Product concentration in three core products — Dimer Acid, Linoleic Acid and Isostearic Acid together contributed 73.1% of value during the year, and the products/services sold table shows a single product line (specialty oleo chemicals) accounting for 94.20% of turnover, so performance is highly sensitive to demand and margin swings in this narrow product set.
- Macro / geopolitical demand risk — Demand moderation from customers was attributed to continual macro uncertainty from U.S.A. tariffs to the recent Middle East war crisis, indicating export and customer demand is exposed to global trade-policy and geopolitical shocks.
- Single manufacturing location — Internal control disclosures note the Company operates with a single operational location, concentrating manufacturing, regulatory and operational risk at one site.
- Exchange rate risk — Identified as one of the categories in the Company's formal Risk Management Policy; relevant given the Company's export revenue (7.80% of turnover in FY2025-26) and stated ambition to grow exports further.
- Country-specific and information/cyber security risk — The Board's Risk Management Policy separately identifies Country specific Risk and Information/Cyber Security Risk, among others (Business, Technological, Financial, Liquidity, Safety, Employee and Natural Calamity risks), as factors that in the Board's opinion could threaten the Company's existence.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Dimer Acid: ~30% of revenue (Rs. 140cr); Linoleic Acid: ~30% of revenue; Isosteric Acid: ~5-6% (Rs. 26cr), high-margin cosmetic grade with long validation cycle; Bypass Fat: New plant operational next month (Q1FY27), revenue from Q3FY27.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as one of a kind manufacturing process using by-products of vegetable oils generated in very small quantities of ~1.25% (for Acid Oil) and ~0.25% (for DOD) of soft oils processed, with 30 years of legacy.
- Promoted by Fairfax India Holdings and backed by an experienced management team; positioned as the leading manufacturer in India for a substantial part of overall revenue and as enjoying a leadership position due to barriers to entry.
- Claims well entrenched customer relationships in high growth industries like Paint, Printing Inks, lubricants and Cosmetics, with customer relationships of more than 15 years and more than 20 years relationships with key raw material suppliers.
- Positions itself as a "Make-in-India, Buy within India" business — the vast majority of raw material and finished products are procured or sold (in case of domestic sales) within a radius of 500 Km of the Sanand facility.
- States it is in a position to market the entire quantity of Prime Products it produces.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Trade policy] Deck flags the recent announcement of level playing tariff with the US and proposed FTA with EU/UK as augering well for the export strategy, and cites lower tariff in the US, FTA with the UK, likely FTA with the EU and recent rupee devaluation as likely to improve capacity utilization during the year, while noting macros are uncertain due to the middle east crisis.
- [Governance] Current auditors are KPMG, and the company states it has been audited by one of the Big 4 for the last 9 years; board includes independent directors Venkatraman Srinivasan, Darius Dinshaw Pandole, Sonal Vimal Ambani and Sudhin Choksey, with Nahoosh Jariwala as Managing Director and Chairman and Sumit Maheshwari as Non-Executive Director.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 63.26%, FPI 6.34%, AIF 2.02%, Public 28.38%.
- [Import substitution] Deck attributes better domestic realisation to lower imports due to supply chain constraints, indicating import competition is a key swing factor for domestic pricing.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Fairchem Organics manufactures specialty Oleo Chemicals - principally Dimer Acid, Linoleic Acid / Soya Fatty Acid, Isostearic Acid, Monobasic Acid, Palmitic Acid and other Distilled Fatty Acids - by processing by-products of vegetable-oil refineries into higher-grade fatty acids. It also produces (natural) Tocopherols and Sterols, intermediate nutraceuticals that are exclusively exported. It operates a Business-to-Business model, selling to manufacturers of epoxy hardeners, paints, printing inks, adhesives, lubricants, cosmetics, soaps, animal feed, pet food and pharma products.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% in Q4 (vs 3.6% in Q4FY25) driven by 8-10% price realization gain due to reduced Chinese dumping and energy cost savings (Rs. 60cr in Q4 vs Rs. 80cr prior year). Raw material (vegetable oil) prices stable; power/fuel costs down due to equipment upgrades.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting 75-80% capacity utilization in FY27 (vs 65% in FY26); Margin: Targeting 8% EBITDA in FY27, potential for double-digits long-term; Order Inflow: Export share to rise from 9% to 20% in 12-14 months; Capex: Minimal in FY27 (only energy savings), major capex for new product phased over 5 years.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No formal order book; sales are spot/monthly contracts. Demand visibility improving with Chinese import pressure easing (imports dropped from ~1000 tonnes/month to negligible).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Capacity utilization ramp-up from 65% to 95% over 2 years on existing 80kT plant. 2) New novel oleochemical product (40kT potential capacity) commissioning Q2FY27, targeting Rs. 800-1000cr revenue over 5 years with 15-18% margins. 3) Export expansion to US/EU/Japan leveraging FTAs and rupee depreciation.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continuous process and cost optimization and development of new products, while maintaining strong relationships across the complete supply chain
- Exploring technical improvement and process optimization for better yields, product mix and energy efficiency
- Growing export markets for Dimer Acid and for the newly launched Isostearic Acid
- Exploring an opportunity to upgrade the Tocopherols and Sterols product streams when commercially viable
- Maintaining leadership in Dimer Acid via pricing strategy, timely service, quick supply, fair payment terms and product quality
- Company recommends periodic dividends to shareholders, subject to AGM approval (Final Dividend of Re. 1 / 10% per equity share proposed for FY2025-26); dividends are also paid to promoter-group entities (FIH Mauritius Investments Limited, FIH Private Investments Limited, Nahoosh Tradelink LLP, Jariwala Tradelink LLP), consistent with a governance framework in which the Fairfax Group, as ultimate holding company, exercises Board oversight through its nominee director alongside a majority-independent Non-Executive Board.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: No new plant, line or capacity-expansion project with a commissioning/completion timeline is disclosed in this bundle. The Company successfully launched its in-house developed, high-value Isostearic Acid product in the international market during the year, with an encouraging initial response. As part of its environmental strategy it continues to implement a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system to capture, treat and reuse all water and liquid waste generated by operations, supported by targeted capex investment aimed at resource efficiency and reduced water consumption; solid-waste management from production processes has also been improved.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for biodegradable chemicals from natural sources is supporting growth of the oleo chemicals market
- Rising demand from printing inks, adhesives and paper-coatings industries expected to drive demand for non-reactive polyamide (Dimer Acid) applications
- Increasing surface-coatings and adhesives demand in marine and construction expected to drive reactive-polyamide applications
- FY2025-26 performance was impacted by higher raw material cost not fully passed through to finished-product pricing, and by demand moderation from customers amid macro uncertainty from U.S.A. tariffs and the Middle East war crisis
- Management is 'consciously optimistic' about FY2026-27 export competitiveness due to lower U.S. tariffs, a likely FTA with the UK and EU, and recent rupee devaluation
- India's dependence on imported crude vegetable oils (from Indonesia, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Ukraine, Russia) exposes raw-material pricing to those countries' export policy shifts and geopolitical disruption
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Fairchem Organics has bottomed out in Q4FY26 as Chinese dumping abated and paint demand recovered, driving a margin rebound to 6.9% despite a 3.2% revenue decline. The core investment thesis pivots on restoring 80% capacity utilization in FY27 and the phased commissioning (FY27-28) of a novel high-margin product line targeting $1B+ revenue potential over five years.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Leading Indian manufacturer of specialty Oleo Chemicals (fatty acids) and intermediate nutraceuticals, holding a leadership position in Dimer Acid and the only Indian maker of paint-grade Linoleic Acid and Isostearic Acid.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Fairchem Organics manufactures specialty Oleo Chemicals - principally Dimer Acid, Linoleic Acid / Soya Fatty Acid, Isostearic Acid, Monobasic Acid, Palmitic Acid and other Distilled Fatty Acids - by processing by-products of vegetable-oil refineries into higher-grade fatty acids. It also produces (natural) Tocopherols and Sterols, intermediate nutraceuticals that are exclusively exported. It operates a Business-to-Business model, selling to manufacturers of epoxy hardeners, paints, printing inks, adhesives, lubricants, cosmetics, soaps, animal feed, pet food and pharma products.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for biodegradable chemicals from natural sources is supporting growth of the oleo chemicals market
- Rising demand from printing inks, adhesives and paper-coatings industries expected to drive demand for non-reactive polyamide (Dimer Acid) applications
- Increasing surface-coatings and adhesives demand in marine and construction expected to drive reactive-polyamide applications
- FY2025-26 performance was impacted by higher raw material cost not fully passed through to finished-product pricing, and by demand moderation from customers amid macro uncertainty from U.S.A. tariffs and the Middle East war crisis
- Management is 'consciously optimistic' about FY2026-27 export competitiveness due to lower U.S. tariffs, a likely FTA with the UK and EU, and recent rupee devaluation
- India's dependence on imported crude vegetable oils (from Indonesia, Malaysia, Brazil, Argentina, Ukraine, Russia) exposes raw-material pricing to those countries' export policy shifts and geopolitical disruption

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: No new plant, line or capacity-expansion project with a commissioning/completion timeline is disclosed in this bundle. The Company successfully launched its in-house developed, high-value Isostearic Acid product in the international market during the year, with an encouraging initial response. As part of its environmental strategy it continues to implement a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system to capture, treat and reuse all water and liquid waste generated by operations, supported by targeted capex investment aimed at resource efficiency and reduced water consumption; solid-waste management from production processes has also been improved.

management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledged 'washed out' last two years but emphasized structural turnaround via dumping cessation and operational efficiencies. Confident on 8% margin target and long-term vision.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leadership position in the Indian Dimer Acid market, built on pricing strategy, timely service, quick supply, fair payment terms and quality, against Chinese suppliers as main competitors
- Ability to process by-products with no fixed technical specification into higher-grade fatty acids and intermediate nutraceuticals meeting stringent quality standards
- Strong, long-standing customer and supplier relationships of more than 25 years
- First Indian and reportedly first Asian company to manufacture Isostearic Acid to internationally acceptable quality without importing technology or external consultants, in a field with only 3-4 global manufacturers
- Only Indian company producing the grade of Linoleic Acid needed for superior-grade paints, making it the preferred supplier for that use
- Natural structural barrier to new entrants: limited domestic availability of key raw materials and unviable import economics under prevailing duties make the market suited to essentially one large domestic player

other.body:
- [Trade policy] Deck flags the recent announcement of level playing tariff with the US and proposed FTA with EU/UK as augering well for the export strategy, and cites lower tariff in the US, FTA with the UK, likely FTA with the EU and recent rupee devaluation as likely to improve capacity utilization during the year, while noting macros are uncertain due to the middle east crisis.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
